coverage.objective: Observation, hypothesis and experiment defined, and the parts of an experiment: aim, apparatus/materials, method or procedure, result, conclusion

evidence.explanation: Observation (29) is 'the use of human senses to describe an observation by using the characteristics and properties of material', with the same block pointing on from observation to classification, inference, measurement and identification. Hypothesis (30) is 'a sensible proposal or reasonable assumption or a scientific guess that can be subjected to verification or being tested'. Experiment (31) is 'the process used for testing of hypothesis through experimentation during which data are collected', which defines the thing in terms of itself.

The parts of an experiment are given one line each: AIM (33) 'the purpose for which the experiment is carried out'; APPARATUS//MATERIALS (34) 'the materials that will be used for the experiment'; METHOD or PROCEDURE (35) 'used to describe the details that are required step by step'; RESULT (36) 'the record of what is seen during and after the experiment'; CONCLUSION (37) 'used to finalize the outcome of the whole experiment'. They are numbered (iv)-(viii), continuing the (i)-(iii) of blocks 29-31, so the source presents the parts of an experiment as peers of observation, hypothesis and experiment itself. No experiment, apparatus list, quantity or safety instruction is given anywhere in blocks 13-41; the first experiments with materials in this document are the Week 5 experiments I-V at blocks 714-765, and this item invents none.
